title: Choose the landing page's structure
question: The world is already pinned — grid motif, neutral ground, cool-tinged dark and faintly warm light. So this choice is composition: how the page argues. The roll dealt three structures and put The Working Rail in the lead.

options.label: The Working Rail
options.lineage: the product's own filter interface, promoted to the page's spine
options.thesis: The page is the tool, running. A filter rail holds the left edge for the entire scroll and visibly culls a corpus down to what is actually yours.
options.viewport: A dense unfiltered corpus field on the grid, a running count above it, and the rail already narrowing it as you arrive.
options.risk: A rail that animates on scroll without the student's hand on it can read as a canned demo reel rather than a tool.
options.case: Filter-richness is the confirmed operating context, and for a prototype the most honest available proof is the interface visibly doing its job. Effort-to-return, the tag matrix and match scoring all enter as rail dimensions the student watches work, so all four mechanisms arrive as one argument instead of four claims. Ends with the rail collapsing into a sign-up.

options.label: The Deadline Wall
options.lineage: a wall-mounted term planner, deadlines as vertical marks
options.thesis: Time is the axis. A horizontal wall of deadlines runs the page, each application a bar weighing work still owed against days still left.
options.viewport: The wall itself, edge to edge, with three bars already inside the seven-day band and their remaining work visible.
options.risk: Leads with pressure. Argue urgency too hard and the page reads as another site telling a student they are already behind.
options.case: Finishing beats finding is a stated product principle, and this is the only structure that makes it the spine rather than a closing section. The pipeline leads, and scoring, tags and the vault become the instruments for surviving the wall. Strongest structure if the sharpest pain you want to name is unfinished applications, not undiscovered ones.

options.label: The Cascade
options.lineage: a sorting cascade — each screen drops what no longer qualifies
options.thesis: You are the query. The page starts with an empty profile and a huge corpus, then narrows visibly with every fact you'd enter until only what is genuinely yours is left standing.
options.viewport: An empty three-field profile against a count in the thousands, the first fact landing and the count dropping as you watch.
options.risk: The counts are mock. Numbers this prominent must be labeled as a demonstration or the page overstates a corpus that does not exist.
options.case: Answers the feeling this student actually arrives with — that the billions in scholarships are never for them. The eligibility tag matrix becomes the structure rather than a feature, and the narrowing dramatizes structured eligibility better than any explanation of it. Ends on a small honest set of matches and an account to claim them.

regions.label: cascade: each fact culls the field
